nodes.label: package() PluginPackage export
nodes.rationale: A file on disk is not enough; the host only sees packages listed from user/lib.rs.

nodes.label: packages() registry
nodes.rationale: Declaring the module or listing it in packages() alone can still compile while the plugin never loads.

nodes.label: Host callback wiring
nodes.rationale: Skipping evaluator, autocomplete, hover, command, YAML, or grammar wiring is the usual reason a buffer opens but evaluate or completions do nothing.

nodes.label: External plugin stub
nodes.rationale: The page allows that an external tool might drop a stub module, but Volt ships no generator and names no such tool.

nodes.label: Autocomplete source or-group
nodes.rationale: Providers in the same or-group compete; once a higher-priority provider returns results, lower ones in that group are skipped.

nodes.label: Workspace lint policy
nodes.rationale: Workspace lints forbid unsafe_code and deny dbg!, todo!, and unwrap() so clippy stays clean before changes are submitted.

nodes.label: workspace.compile
nodes.rationale: The command stages a unique copy under volt-user-hot because a mapped DLL cannot be overwritten in place on Windows.

nodes.label: PluginAction
nodes.rationale: Richer behavior goes through hooks that the host or other packages already understand, beyond log_message, open_buffer, and emit_hook.

nodes.label: In-process volt API
nodes.rationale: New host capabilities are authored against editor-plugin-api, not internal crates/editor-* paths.

nodes.label: No plugin scaffold CLI
nodes.rationale: cargo xtask has no scaffold CLI, so creating a plugin is a manual module, package() export, and lib.rs registration.

nodes.label: Mapped user.dll staging
nodes.rationale: Staging avoids overwriting a mapped library. That matters especially on Windows, where a loaded user.dll cannot be replaced in place.

nodes.label: ADR 0008 User Source Tree and Plugin SDK boundary
Hot-reload ABI fallback
nodes.rationale: Hot-reloaded cdylib copies may fall back to host-side workers for some capabilities until non-prefix ABI seams exist. Prefer rebuilding against a matching SDK when host APIs change.

nodes.label: editor-plugin-api SDK
nodes.rationale: The SDK is the only stable ABI boundary. Builtin plugins author against the SDK plus crates.io, not internal engine crates.

nodes.label: DEFAULT_THEME_ID gruvbox-dark
nodes.rationale: Changing the default theme id constant requires rebuilding volt-user. Switching themes interactively does not.

nodes.label: global.toml shared options
nodes.rationale: user/themes/global.toml holds font, scrolloff, language defaults, and window transparency, and is not a selectable theme.

nodes.label: Theme pallet and tokens
nodes.rationale: Named theme files map tokens to palette colors. Both pallet and palette are accepted section names.

nodes.label: ui.yaml terminal program
nodes.rationale: Prefer YAML so the shell change applies at runtime without rebuilding the user package.

nodes.label: Platform default terminal
nodes.rationale: If program is empty, Volt falls back to the platform default compiled into the user library.

nodes.label: Shell UI backend flag
nodes.rationale: Default UI remains SDL. --ui=sdl keeps the SDL3 shell. --ui=gpui (alias --ui=gupi) paints the same editor scene in a GPUI window. The embedded browser stays SDL-only.

nodes.label: user/config.yaml master table
nodes.rationale: Day-to-day YAML can change behavior without rebuilding volt-user. The master file is a reference table of child paths, not a YAML include. Rust commands, hooks, and keybindings still need a rebuild.

nodes.label: Per-plugin YAML config
nodes.rationale: Parsing stays centralized in user/config.rs so every plugin shares one schema and reload path.

nodes.label: SDL and GPUI UI backends
nodes.rationale: The embedded browser webview stays on the SDL shell and is skipped in GPUI mode. A second --ui flag or an unknown value is an error, and --ui=gpui cannot be combined with --bootstrap-demo.

nodes.label: user/ customization layout
nodes.rationale: Rust package metadata needs a rebuild. YAML under user/config and theme TOML under user/themes hot-reload.

nodes.label: Volt modal editor
nodes.rationale: The home page describes Volt as a modal editor with a layered, programmable core covering architecture, user packages, and in-editor help.

nodes.label: Client-side TF-IDF docs search
nodes.rationale: Search ranks natural-language questions with TF-IDF in the browser, with no AI and no server, and is what the in-editor help command opens.

nodes.label: lang common helper
nodes.rationale: The helper builds a standard attach command, file-open hook binding, and syntax configuration. The page says to copy a recent module that already uses it, but does not name that module.
